questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: She [don't] like coffee.
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'She' takes 'doesn't'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: He [go] to school every day.
questions.explanation: Third-person singular in the present simple takes 'goes'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: They [is playing] football.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'They' takes 'are playing'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: I have [saw] that movie.
questions.explanation: The present perfect needs the past participle 'seen'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: The [childrens] are happy.
questions.explanation: 'Children' is already plural; 'childrens' is incorrect.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: She is [more taller] than her sister.
questions.explanation: 'Taller' is already comparative; 'more' is redundant.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: He [did not went] there.
questions.explanation: After 'did not' the base verb 'go' is used.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: [Me and my friend] went out.
questions.explanation: As the subject, the correct form is 'My friend and I'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: There [is many people] here.
questions.explanation: Plural 'people' takes 'are many people'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: He [is knowing] the answer.
questions.explanation: 'Know' is a stative verb and is not used in the continuous; use 'knows'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: She sang very [good].
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify 'sang': 'well'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: This is the [most best] option.
questions.explanation: 'Best' is already superlative; 'most' is redundant.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: He is [senior than] me.
questions.explanation: 'Senior' is followed by 'to', not 'than'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: One should do [his] duty.
questions.explanation: The pronoun must agree with 'one': use 'one's'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: [Hardly I had] reached when the train left.
questions.explanation: After 'Hardly' the auxiliary is inverted: 'Hardly had I'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: The scenery of Kashmir [are] beautiful.
questions.explanation: 'Scenery' is uncountable and takes the singular 'is'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: He prefers tea [than] coffee.
questions.explanation: 'Prefer' is followed by 'to', not 'than'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: She has been ill [since three days].
questions.explanation: With a duration, use 'for': 'for three days'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: Each of the boys [have] a pen.
questions.explanation: 'Each of' takes a singular verb: 'has'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: I am used to [get up] early.
questions.explanation: 'Used to' (habit) is followed by a gerund: 'getting up'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: He is one of the best [student] in the class.
questions.explanation: 'One of the best' is followed by a plural noun: 'students'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: [If I was] you, I would accept the offer.
questions.explanation: In an unreal condition, use the subjunctive 'If I were'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: Neither he nor his friends [was] present.
questions.explanation: With 'neither ... nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'friends' (plural): 'were'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: He asked [that where I was] going.
questions.explanation: An indirect question drops 'that' and keeps statement order: 'where I was'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: No sooner did he arrive [than] the meeting started.
questions.explanation: 'No sooner ... than' is the correct pair, so no improvement is needed.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: The reason for his failure [is because] he was careless.
questions.explanation: 'The reason ... is because' is redundant; use 'is that'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: He is [more cleverer] than his brother.
questions.explanation: 'Cleverer' is already comparative; 'more' is redundant.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: I look forward to [meet] you soon.
questions.explanation: In 'look forward to', 'to' is a preposition and is followed by a gerund: 'meeting'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: She could not [help but to laugh].
questions.explanation: 'Cannot help' is followed by a gerund: 'help laughing'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: Ten miles [are] a long distance to walk.
questions.explanation: A measured distance is treated as a single unit: 'is'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: He behaves [as if he was] a king.
questions.explanation: After 'as if' expressing an unreal idea, use the subjunctive 'were'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: The teacher along with the students [were] present.
questions.explanation: 'Along with' does not change the number of the subject 'teacher' (singular): use 'was'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: I have been [knowing] him for years.
questions.explanation: 'Know' is stative; the present perfect 'have known' is correct.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: Please [explain me the problem].
questions.explanation: 'Explain' takes 'to' before the person: 'explain the problem to me'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: He is [too tired that] he cannot walk.
questions.explanation: The 'so ... that' construction is required: 'so tired that'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: [Not only he came] but also stayed for dinner.
questions.explanation: When a sentence begins with 'Not only', the auxiliary is inverted: 'Not only did he come'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: The committee [were unanimous in their] decision.
questions.explanation: Taken as a single body, 'committee' is singular: 'was unanimous in its'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: [Had I known] about the strike, I would have left earlier.
questions.explanation: The inverted third conditional 'Had I known' is correct, so no improvement is needed.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: He knew the answer, [isn't it]?
questions.explanation: The question tag must match the statement's verb and subject: 'didn't he?'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: Scarcely had he left [than] it began to rain.
questions.explanation: 'Scarcely ... when' is the correct pair (not 'than').

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: The number of road accidents [have] increased this year.
questions.explanation: 'The number of' is singular: use 'has increased'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: He would rather die [than to beg].
questions.explanation: 'Would rather ... than' is followed by the bare infinitive: 'than beg'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: He worked hard [lest he should fail].
questions.explanation: 'Lest ... should' is the correct construction, so no improvement is needed.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: The more you earn, [more you spend].
questions.explanation: The correlative comparative needs 'the' in both clauses: 'the more you spend'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: It is high time we [leave] for the airport.
questions.explanation: 'It is high time' is followed by the past subjunctive: 'left'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: He is [capable to do] this difficult work.
questions.explanation: 'Capable' is followed by 'of' + gerund: 'capable of doing'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: I wish I [was] taller.
questions.explanation: After 'wish' expressing an unreal present, use the subjunctive 'were'.

questions.stem: Improve the bracketed part: The teacher said that the earth [moved] round the sun.
questions.explanation: A universal truth stays in the present tense even in reported speech: 'moves'.
